So this app I'm using has some challenges that I thought I'd want to do and I found a "30 Day Asexuality Challenge" and since I don't talk about that part of me much, I'm gonna do it here!

Day 1: Romantic/Sexual Orientation I am definitely aroace, long before I knew the term. I get squishes but I thought they were like....full fledged romantic attraction until I actually really read up on it a while back.

Day 3: When did you realize you were asexual? What made you realize it? It was after I got into a relationship with my friend at 19. I had a squish on him but I thought it was romantic attraction. It made me realize I didn't want to be in a romantic relationship and never did.

Day 3: When did you realize you were asexual? What made you realize it? It was after I got into a relationship with my friend at 19. I had a squish on him but I thought it was romantic attraction. It made me realize I didn't want to be in a romantic relationship and never did.

Day 4: Do you identify as part of the LGBT+ community? What communities do you identify with? I'm not sure I can say I do, though I did before and I still want to be a part of it. But with members not wanting ace people in it and discourse happening about it, I'm hesitant.

But communities I DO identify with are feminist communities and the asian community. I don't live in USA so it's different from American POC communities, but I relate quite well with other asians, especially those in southeast.

I was telling her about the different kinds of sexualities and romantic orientations and when I talked about asexuality, she really identified with it. Because of that, I shared to her that I was aroace.
i got to asexuality in 6 clicks from this article about a flightless weevil

Day 6: Have you faced oppression because of your asexuality? I only share my sexuality with a handful of people IRL so I haven't really come across any real problems. My parents used to insist that we eventually get married and have kids but they've learned to accept us.

Day 8: Thoughts on Asexual Pride I do want to be part of pride but yeah, there's definitely a rocky relationship with LGBT+ people. I don't think we need pride specifically but I do think it'd be a good idea to have a sort of event aces can just be with fellows and supporters.

Day 9: The Meaning of Being Asexual to You It means that no matter what age you are, people will keep asking you about getting together with someone and having to explain again and again. But it also means that those who know and still love you really understand and love you.

Day 10: What others have said about your Asexuality Generally my friends have been very understanding. I don't come out to them unless I know they're open about it. As for my family, my parents definitely thought it was a phase or just my inexperience but they're getting around.

Day 12: Favorite Asexual Tumblr/Blog I never really followed blogs that were strictly asexual in Tumblr but if on Twitter, I'd have to go with . It feels very intimate and real, plus it feels like such a good resource of asexual and/or aromantic content.

Day 13: Favorite Asexual Site I'd have to go with , right? It's one of first resources for ace people and has a pretty extensive FAQ for aces, those who are questioning, or just want to learn more about asexuality. Plus, the forum it hosts is pretty extensive as well.

Asexuality means to me that I'm not incomplete or that there's something missing. I realized I wasn't just "a late bloomer" or that there was something wrong about me because I didn't want to be in a relationship or have sex. But most importantly, it means that I'm not alone.

Day 14: Another Asexual You've Met The first ace I met was someone I met online through the hijack fandom. We really hit it off, even if I didn't know I was ace. They became one of the closest people I knew online and I loved them to pieces. I just lost connection with them.

Day 15: Favorite Character/Celebrity/Person I can't say I have a favorite asexual /person/ but I was pretty happy to find out Tim Gunn was asexual. I don't really know much about him or fashion in general but I love an icon who I can relate to.

Day 16: Favorite "Asexual" Book (wherein sex/romance is not the main focus) I've bought books about aro/ace characters but since I haven't read them, I'll have to go with an "asexual" book. I adore Neverwhere by Neil Gaiman. I love the author and it's just such a good concept.

Day 17: Favorite "Asexual" Film (wherein sex/romance is not the main focus) I absolutely love The Iron Giant. It was one of my favorite films when I was young but also there's something relatable about the giant and his sacrifice gets me every fucking time.

Day 22: Favorite Asexual Pride Image/Symbol Of course, I have a soft spot for the flag because it's the best symbol for asexuality. But I also really like the spade symbol because it was one of the first symbols that really left an impression on me as I was starting to identify.
